overview: This file documents an extended 1946–47 State Department dispute over French demands for approximately $37.3 million in gold earmarked in Tokyo by wartime Japan for the Saigon branch of the Bank of Indochina. Officials agreed that earmarking might have transferred legal title but disagreed sharply over whether the transactions represented legitimate payment, compensation extracted under duress, or a reward for Vichy French collaboration with Japan. The discussions compare the French claim with larger Siamese gold credits, Japanese reparations and restitution policy, occupation financing, European precedents for monetary gold, and the political status of French Indochina and Siam during the war. The file ends without a definitive settlement, with proposals ranging from outright refusal, through partial release based on the date of earmarking, to provisional delivery subject to review by the Far Eastern Commission.

subfiles.title: Martin memorandum on the French request for earmarked gold
subfiles.to: Alwyn V. Freeman, Office of the Legal Adviser
subfiles.about: Reports the initial French presentation and requests legal and political advice on releasing gold earmarked in Japan for the Saigon branch of the Bank of Indochina.
subfiles.summary: Martin: French officials claim $37.3 million in Japan-earmarked gold as legitimate wartime payment, not reparations or loot, noting a similar Siamese case.

subfiles.title: Freeman legal opinion on the French gold claim
subfiles.from: Alwyn V. Freeman, Office of the Legal Adviser
subfiles.about: Assesses whether Japanese earmarking transferred legal title to the French and whether broader policy considerations nevertheless justified withholding the gold.
subfiles.summary: Freeman finds FEC restitution rules don't clearly cover the earmarked gold, but argues Vichy's collaboration might still justify withholding it on policy grounds.

subfiles.title: Robinson memorandum requesting political comment on French gold
subfiles.to: John Carter Vincent, FE; H. Freeman Matthews, EUR
subfiles.about: Solicits Far Eastern and European political views on the French demand for release of $37.3 million in gold.
subfiles.summary: Robinson reports SCAP is gathering Japanese records; a tentative view would treat only pre-occupation gold as legitimate commerce, leaving later gold to reparations.

subfiles.title: Metzger memorandum on gold found at the German Legation in China
subfiles.about: Recommends returning gold found at the German Legation to China while asking China to hold it for IARA if its German origin is established.
subfiles.summary: Metzger argues China should be invited to accede to the gold resolution rather than have it applied automatically.

subfiles.title: Martin memorandum on French wartime status and the gold claim
subfiles.to: John Carter Vincent, FE; H. Freeman Matthews, EUR
subfiles.about: Frames the gold and reparations questions around the wartime status of French authorities in Indochina.
subfiles.summary: Martin weighs whether Indochina's wartime status was neutral, puppet, belligerent, or collaborative, proposing to deny gold claims from the collaboration period and date belligerency to October 1944.

subfiles.title: Vincent memorandum comparing French Indochinese and Siamese gold
subfiles.about: Argues that the United States should apply the same policy to French Indochinese and Siamese gold credits established while their governments aided Japan.
subfiles.summary: Vincent proposes forfeiting French and Siamese credits created under wartime duress, while releasing credits from before or after those periods, with equal treatment for both.

subfiles.title: Annex A: wartime status of French Indochina
subfiles.about: Provides a chronology supporting the view that French Indochina collaborated under duress from August 1940 and became belligerent against Japan only in March 1945.
subfiles.summary: Annex concludes Indochina's August 1940 agreement with Japan began collaboration, with belligerent status only applying after Japan ousted French rule in March 1945.

subfiles.title: Annex B: wartime status of Siam
subfiles.about: Reviews Siam's alliance and material assistance to Japan and the emergence of a resistance movement prepared to act against the Japanese in 1945.
subfiles.summary: Annex on Siam: describes its 1941 duress agreement and 1942 war declaration, concluding resistance was ready by May 1945 but held back at Allied request.

subfiles.title: Reber memorandum on the starting date for forfeiture
subfiles.to: H. Freeman Matthews, EUR; John Carter Vincent, FE
subfiles.about: Concurs with forfeiting wartime gold credits but questions whether Japan could legally be called an enemy before December 1941.
subfiles.summary: Reber proposes dating French Indochina's forfeiture period from December 1941, when the US entered the war, not August 1940.

subfiles.title: Hilldring recommendation to treat French gold as reparations
subfiles.about: Recommends rejecting immediate French ownership claims and treating the earmarked gold solely as a reparations matter.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring recommends denying France's $37.3 million gold claim, warning it would invite a Siamese claim and favor France unfairly.

subfiles.title: Ness memorandum supporting release of the French gold
subfiles.to: Willard L. Thorp, A-T; John H. Hilldring, A-H
subfiles.about: Opposes JK's recommendation and urges American support for releasing the earmarked gold to France.
subfiles.summary: Ness argues for releasing the French gold via FEC or SCAP, citing international norms on monetary-gold transfers and noting denial wouldn't help reparations claimants.

subfiles.title: Ness note on Treasury opposition
subfiles.to: Willard L. Thorp, A-T; John H. Hilldring, A-H
subfiles.about: Reports that the Treasury Department would strongly oppose any refusal to release the Indochinese gold.
subfiles.summary: Ness adds that Treasury would strongly oppose withholding the gold from France.

subfiles.title: Vincent memorandum proposing a chronological compromise
subfiles.to: Willard L. Thorp, A-T; John H. Hilldring, A-H
subfiles.about: Proposes releasing only French and Siamese gold earmarked before the countries entered periods of collaboration with Japan.
subfiles.summary: Vincent proposes a compromise date, releasing some French and Siamese gold while treating later credits as reparations.

subfiles.title: Surrey legal comments on the Indochinese gold
subfiles.from: W. S. Surrey, Office of the Legal Adviser
subfiles.about: Concludes that the ultimate issue is political but that France probably has the stronger legal claim to the earmarked gold.
subfiles.summary: Surrey argues duress didn't bar Indochina's claim to the gold and finds no clear legal precedent, calling the decision essentially political.

subfiles.title: War Department transmittal of SCAP report on Thai gold
subfiles.from: Ray J. Lane for Major General Daniel Noce, War Department Civil Affairs Division
subfiles.to: John H. Hilldring, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits SCAP's response concerning the circumstances, quantity, identification, and status of gold earmarked for Siamese account.
subfiles.summary: War Department forwards SCAP's report on Japanese gold earmarked for Thailand, responding to a State Department request.

subfiles.title: McGuire memorandum opposing release to France
subfiles.about: Forcefully rejects OFD's release recommendation and argues that the gold represented a Japanese reward for Vichy collaboration.
subfiles.summary: McGuire opposes releasing gold to France, arguing it unfairly rewards wartime collaborators over resisting nations, and recommends compensating France through ordinary reparations instead.

subfiles.title: Saltzman memorandum on referral to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.to: Robert A. Lovett, Under Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Recommends referring the French claim to the Far Eastern Commission or making any urgent delivery provisional and reversible.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman favors FEC review of the gold claim, suggesting conditional delivery to France with repayment if later ruled otherwise.

interest: Shows a postwar US dispute over whether Japanese-held French and Siamese gold was legitimate payment or wartime loot.
